title: Sunny and the Magpie Lullaby | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka hears a single magpie singing very softly in the moonlight — not its usual carol but something quieter, lower, meant only for the night — and wonders if it is singing the bush to sleep. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
A magpie was singing in the dark.

Not the full, bright carol it saved for mornings — Sunny knew that sound well, loud and liquid and meant to carry across the whole paddock. This was something else. Softer. Slower. A sound made for the middle of the night.

She found the magpie in a low branch of a paperbark tree, its black and white feathers silvered by the moonlight. It was singing with its beak barely open, the notes coming out quiet and round and almost private.

She stood very still.

The notes moved up and down in a slow rolling pattern. Not a melody she could follow exactly — it wandered, looped back, went somewhere new. But it had a shape. Something gentle and inevitable, the way a river has a shape even when you can't see all of it at once.

She thought: it is singing the bush to sleep.

She sat down at the base of the paperbark.

The magpie continued its soft song, looking at nothing, looking at everything. It had been singing, probably, since long before she arrived. It would keep singing, probably, long after she fell asleep.

The notes settled around her like something warm.

She leaned back against the bark.

The song went on. Soft and round and private.

And it sang her to sleep.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, magpie. Goodnight, little one.
